problem_statement: Return True if n is a perfect square (there exists an integer k such that k * k equals n), otherwise False. n is any Python integer (excluding bool). Negative numbers are not perfect squares.
valid_input_domain: Return True if n is a perfect square (there exists an integer k such that k * k equals n), otherwise False. n is any Python integer (excluding bool). Negative numbers are not perfect squares.
bug_explanation: The faulty solution uses k * k <= n instead of k * k < n, so k overshoots the square root and the final equality check always fails for perfect squares.
provenance: Custom main-study task, drafted with AI assistance. Not copied from a benchmark; no novelty claim.
